units.summary: Adds errorCacheTTL = 5 minutes, which controls how long a failed inventory lookup is reused before the server is asked again. The comment explains it with permanently forbidden records, but GetRecord applies the TTL to every kind of error.
units.headline: Adds a 5-minute TTL for cached inventory lookup failures
units.reason: A new tunable decides how long lookups stay suppressed after a failure, which changes runtime behaviour.
focus: Check that 5 minutes is acceptable for transient failures too, not only FORBIDDEN replies

units.summary: New struct that holds a failed lookup's error and its expiry time. It is a data holder only; the behaviour lives in GetRecord.
units.headline: Adds a struct holding a cached error and its expiry
units.reason: Plain unexported data type; it only matters through GetRecord, which is reviewed separately.

units.summary: Client gains an errors map plus get and now function fields that tests can replace. The type has no JSON or wire use, but each new map is another piece of shared mutable state with no lock.
units.headline: Client gains an error cache and injectable fetch and clock functions
units.reason: Changes struct fields that hold mutable state and route all record fetches.
focus: Whether Track (and so GetRecord) can run concurrently; neither the cache map nor the new errors map has a lock

units.summary: NewClient now creates the errors map, sets now to time.Now and points get at fetchFromServer. All fields are set, so nothing can be nil at use.
units.headline: Constructor sets up the error map, clock and fetch function
units.reason: Straightforward setup of the new fields; nothing is left uninitialized.

units.summary: Drops the retry parameter. Any error from get is now cached per key for errorCacheTTL and returned again without calling the server. Successful results are still cached forever.

issues.title: Transient errors are cached for 5 minutes, not just FORBIDDEN
issues.failure_scenario: The inventory server is briefly unreachable, or a lookup hits the 1s requestTimeout. The connect or deadline error is cached, so every Track of that key for the next 5 minutes gets no owner. loadMetadata swallows the error and Track stores that metadata with no later refresh, so those items stay without an owner.

issues.title: New errors map has no lock, same as the existing cache
issues.failure_scenario: If Track runs from several goroutines, loadMetadata runs outside l.mu, so concurrent GetRecord calls write the maps at the same time and Go can crash with a fatal concurrent map write. The cache map already had this problem before the PR.

units.headline: GetRecord caches every lookup failure per key for 5 minutes
units.reason: Changes error handling and retry semantics, and changes a method signature.
focus: Whether only ReplyError (permanent) failures should be cached, not timeouts or connection errors
How a cached failure combines with Track storing metadata once (the owner is never filled in later)
Other callers of GetRecord broken by the removed retry parameter

units.summary: Moves the connect-and-get logic here and replaces the recursion with a loop. It reconnects at most once on transport errors and no longer reconnects when the server sent an error reply.
units.headline: Fetch reconnects once on transport errors, never on error replies
units.reason: Changes the retry/reconnect policy for network calls.
focus: A ReplyError leaves the connection open; confirm the conn is reusable after an error reply

units.summary: Uses errors.As to report whether an error is or wraps a ReplyError value. conn.go returns ReplyError by value, so the value-type target matches.
units.headline: Adds a helper that detects inventory server error replies
units.reason: Small helper that matches how conn.go builds the error; tests cover direct and wrapped cases.

units.summary: Updates the call to the new GetRecord signature without the retry flag. Retrying now happens inside fetchFromServer.
units.headline: getRecord call updated for the new GetRecord signature
units.reason: Call-site update only; the retry behaviour moved into fetchFromServer, reviewed separately.
